qs.q: A pediatric patient is diagnosed with phenylketonuria, an autosomal recessive condition. What is the typical underlying molecular defect in this class of Mendelian disorders?
qs.e: Autosomal recessive Mendelian disorders most frequently involve deficiencies in metabolic enzymes, leading to substrate accumulation or product loss.

qs.q: During a review of biochemical genetics, a resident discusses disorders of amino acid metabolism. Phenylketonuria results from a block in converting phenylalanine to which amino acid?
qs.e: Phenylketonuria is caused by deficient phenylalanine hydroxylase, preventing the normal metabolic conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine.

qs.q: A mutation in the gene encoding phenylalanine hydroxylase leads to classic phenylketonuria. If left untreated, why do patients exhibit developmental delay and intellectual disability?
o: Accumulated phenylalanine inhibits transport of other essential amino acids into brain tissue.
Deficient tyrosine synthesis stops production of vital neurotransmitters in synapses.
Phenylketones directly destroy myelin sheaths surrounding central nervous system tracts.
Liver failure results in systemic ammonia toxicity affecting cerebral cortex neurons.
Lack of melanin precursors starves developing neural circuits of necessary pigments.
qs.e: High levels of phenylalanine competitively inhibit neutral amino acid transporters at the blood-brain barrier, starving the brain.

qs.q: A patient with phenylketonuria is placed on a low-phenylalanine diet. Which amino acid becomes essential for this individual?
qs.e: Tyrosine is normally synthesized from phenylalanine, so it becomes essential when phenylalanine hydroxylase is deficient.

qs.q: A newborn screening test for phenylketonuria (PKU) primarily measures elevated levels of which circulating substance?
qs.e: Elevated serum phenylalanine measured via tandem mass spectrometry or the Guthrie test forms the basis of newborn PKU screening. Urine phenylpyruvate is a secondary byproduct seen later in untreated disease.

qs.q: Why is newborn screening for phenylketonuria performed using biochemical techniques?
qs.e: Screening is designed to detect diseases before symptoms appear, such as newborn screening for phenylketonuria. Monitoring is instead used for tracking disease progression or therapy response.
